Name the topics of a fitted model

Source: R/topics.R
name_topics.Rd

name_topics() replaces the label of every topic of a fitted model with the names given, in topic order. The labels that topics() gives are drawn from the data (the most central text of each topic, or its most distinctive terms); once the representative texts of each topic have been read, a short name for what the topic is about, such as the kind of message it holds, communicates the result better.

The names then appear in every table and figure that refers to a topic, including summary(), topic_sizes(), terms(), representatives(), predict(), topic_hierarchy(), and plot(). The model is not refitted; the result is the topic model with its labels replaced.

reduce_topics() drops the names, because merged topics need new ones.

Usage

name_topics(object, labels)

Arguments

object

A topic model fitted by topics().

labels

Character vector of distinct, non-empty names, one per topic, in topic order (topic 1 first).

Value

The topic model with its labels replaced; an object of class sbert_topic_model.

Conditions

An error of class sbert_bad_topic_names when labels is not a character vector of distinct, non-empty, non-missing names, one per topic.

See also

representatives() to read each topic before naming it; topics().

Examples

text <- c(
  "Cats chase mice", "Dogs chase balls",
  "Stocks and bonds trade", "Markets price shares"
)
embeddings <- rbind(c(1, 0), c(0.9, 0.1), c(0, 1), c(0.1, 0.9))
topic_model <- topics(text, n_topics = 2, embeddings = embeddings)
named <- name_topics(topic_model, c("Pets", "Finance"))
topic_sizes(named)
#>   topic   label n_documents proportion
#> 1     1    Pets           2        0.5
#> 2     2 Finance           2        0.5
